At stage-3 donhang, donhang_notifications and donhang_payments are three databases on one PostgreSQL server (Host=db); each service connects only to its own; of the services only payments and payments-migrate use donhang_payments; the db-backup CronJob dumps all three from host db.

claims.text: Signs of a distributed monolith: changes that always touch several services, services released only together, services reading each other's tables, chains of calls where one slow service stalls the rest.
OrderMessage reaches Notifications and Payments through RabbitMQ and waits in a queue, so a slow Notifications does not hold up placing an order.
claims.source_hint: backend.l3.message-broker; STAGE.md @ stage-3 data flow (API -> outbox -> RabbitMQ -> Notifications, Payments)

claims.text: POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/refund on DonHang.Api returns 202 (accepted, not done); Payments saves a pending refund on receiving order.refund-requested, and RefundSender calls the payment gateway (provider) afterwards.
DonHang.Api (and Infrastructure), DonHang.Notifications and DonHang.Payments each reference DonHang.Messaging, which references no Đơn Hàng project and knows no order, payment or email.

claims.text: Each service has its own database and maps no other service's tables, but the shared PostgreSQL server stopping takes all three databases down at once; the services' work needing a database fails together.

claims.text: Because each image has its own entry (newTag, digest), a promotion commit can change one service's tag and leave the others; at stage-3 all six share one commit because CI's publish job builds and pushes them together.
claims.source_hint: Kustomize docs, images field; kustomization.yaml @ stage-3 lines 17-39; STAGE.md 'CI signs the six images the publish job pushes'

claims.text: Consumers read OrderMessage JSON by property name; both Read() methods reject a message without CustomerEmail, so renaming it moves the API, Notifications and Payments in step. A shared class would not avoid it: each service reads the new name only once rebuilt and released.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs System.Text.Json (JsonSerializerOptions.Web, missing property); RefundRequestedConsumer.cs, OrderEventsConsumer.cs Read() @ stage-3

claims.text: ServiceUsesNoDonHangProjectButMessaging runs for OrderEventsConsumer (Notifications) and RefundRequestedConsumer (Payments); it fails when that type's assembly references a DonHang.* assembly other than DonHang.Messaging, e.g. a new DonHang.Shared.

Trade-offs: a shared domain project puts every Order change in every service's next build; reading another's tables makes column changes a change in step; an own message copy limits the tie to fields that cross, at the cost of copies to keep alike.

Choices: keep copies over a shared Order project unless services already change together; if refund changes always span Api and Payments, move shared knowledge to one side or weigh merging; give a service its own server only if its drivers ask.
A container decides where code runs, not what it can change or release without; separate databases remove only the table tie.
